easy.explanation: Verse 2 says, “Out of Zion, the perfection of beauty, God hath shined.”
easy.q: From where does God shine forth?

easy.explanation: God calls the heavens and the earth to witness as He judges His people.
easy.q: Whom does God call as witnesses in judging His people?

easy.explanation: Verse 5 says, “Gather my saints together unto me.”

medium.explanation: Fire devours before Him, and a great tempest surrounds Him.
The heavens declare His righteousness because God Himself is judge.
In this passage, His saints are those who belong faithfully to Him.
medium.q: What does “saints” mean in “Gather my saints together unto me”?

answers: That the judgment is hidden from mankind
That the judgment concerns the whole world
That the judgment applies only to saints
challenge.explanation: The heavens and earth are called as witnesses, giving the judgment a universal scope.
challenge.q: What does the calling of the heavens and earth show about the scope of the judgment?

answers: God's appearing, the calling of witnesses, the gathering of His saints, and heaven's testimony
The gathering of saints, sacrifice, tempest, and prayer
Heaven's testimony, God's appearing, sacrifice, and judgment
challenge.explanation: This is the order of the ideas in verses 1–6.
challenge.q: Which sequence correctly describes the scene?

answers: That He judges His people righteously
challenge.explanation: The heavens declare His righteousness, and God is presented as the judge.
challenge.q: What is emphasized by describing God as judge?

easy.explanation: God says, “Hear, O my people... O Israel.”
easy.q: To whom does God speak at the beginning of the passage?

easy.explanation: He says, “I will not reprove thee for thy sacrifices.”
easy.q: Does God reprove Israel merely for offering sacrifices?

easy.explanation: God declares that the beasts of the forest and the cattle belong to Him.
easy.q: To whom do all the beasts belong?

answers: Because there are no animals in the world
Because all the animals already belong to Him
Because they may never be offered
medium.explanation: The world and all its animals belong to God, so He has no need of them.
medium.q: Why does God not need bullocks and he goats?

medium.explanation: “He goats” means male goats, which are listed among the animals belonging to God.
medium.q: What are “he goats” in the passage?

answers: A need that God must have supplied
medium.explanation: The sacrifice does not satisfy a need in God; it expresses the worshiper's commitment.
medium.q: What does sacrifice express according to this passage?

answers: He does not know what is in the fields
He knows every fowl and beast
challenge.explanation: God says that every fowl and beast is known to Him and belongs to Him.
challenge.q: Which statement supports the claim that God does not depend on sacrifices?

answers: That God does not receive nourishment from sacrifices
challenge.explanation: The question makes clear that God does not need food from sacrificial animals.
challenge.q: What does the question “Will I eat the flesh of bulls, or drink the blood of goats?” emphasize?

answers: A sacrifice does not fill any lack in God
challenge.explanation: Since everything already belongs to God, sacrifice does not supply something He lacks.
challenge.q: What follows from the fact that the world and its fulness belong to God?

paragraphs.title: Thanksgiving, Vows, and Prayer in Trouble

easy.q: What is the worshiper told to offer?

easy.explanation: He is told to pay his vows, meaning to fulfill them.
easy.q: What should a person do with his vows?

answers: Only on a day of joy
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Call upon me in the day of trouble.”
easy.q: When should a person call upon God?

medium.q: What does God promise to do in the day of trouble?

answers: I will rescue thee from trouble
medium.explanation: To deliver means to rescue or bring someone out of trouble.
medium.q: What does “I will deliver thee” mean?

answers: Deliverance removes the need for honor
medium.explanation: God says, “I will deliver thee, and thou shalt glorify me.”
medium.q: What is connected with God's deliverance?

answers: Thanksgiving, fulfilling vows, calling in trouble, and glorifying God
Prayer, forgetting God, thanksgiving, and judgment
challenge.explanation: This is the sequence of worship, prayer, divine deliverance, and glorifying God.
challenge.q: Which sequence describes the way presented in these verses?

answers: That a person turns to God only as a last resort
That a person is called to a relationship of prayer and gratitude
That thanksgiving has no connection with conduct
challenge.explanation: The passage presents both thanksgiving and fulfilled vows, as well as calling upon God in trouble.
challenge.q: What does the combination of thanksgiving and prayer in trouble show?

challenge.explanation: The worshiper is called to give thanks, pay vows, and glorify God.
challenge.q: What human response appears alongside God's promise of deliverance?

easy.q: What does the wicked person hate?

easy.explanation: The passage mentions consenting with a thief and being a partaker with adulterers.
easy.q: In what acts does the wicked person participate?

answers: His brother and his mother's son
easy.explanation: He speaks against his brother and slanders his own mother's son.
easy.q: Against whom does the wicked person speak?

answers: He speaks of God's covenant but does not obey God's words
He has never heard God's laws
medium.explanation: He declares God's statutes but hates instruction and casts God's words behind him.
medium.q: What contradiction appears in the wicked person's behavior?

answers: You speak falsely or maliciously against
medium.explanation: To slander is to speak against someone with false or damaging accusations.
medium.q: What does “slanderest” mean in “thou slanderest thine own mother's son”?

answers: God has kept silence and has not reproved him immediately
The heavens testify in his favor
medium.explanation: He wrongly thinks that God's silence means God is altogether like him.
medium.q: Why does the wicked person think God's silence means approval?

answers: They all show a gap between his words and his conduct
They concern only the worship of God
challenge.explanation: He speaks of God's covenant but steals, joins adulterers, deceives, and slanders others.
challenge.q: What connection exists between the wicked person's evil speech and his other actions?

answers: Silence must not be interpreted as consent
challenge.explanation: The wicked person is wrong to interpret God's silence as agreement with his behavior.
challenge.q: What does God's prolonged silence teach?

answers: Harm to property, purity, speech, and family relationships
challenge.explanation: The passage mentions theft, adultery, deceitful speech, evil, and slander against relatives.
challenge.q: What sequence of harm is described in the passage?

paragraphs.title: Warning and the Way to Salvation

easy.explanation: God says, “Consider this, ye that forget God.”
Verse 23 says, “Whoso offereth praise glorifieth me.”
easy.q: Whom does the person who offers praise glorify?

easy.explanation: The verse promises, “I will shew the salvation of God.”
easy.q: What will God show to the person who orders his conversation aright?

answers: They must not think that delayed punishment frees them from judgment
They must leave the right way
medium.explanation: The warning shows that the absence of immediate punishment does not remove accountability.
medium.q: What are those who forget God warned about?

answers: He directs his conduct in the right way
medium.explanation: The phrase describes someone who orders his life and conduct properly.
medium.q: What does “ordereth his conversation aright” mean in this context?

answers: Praise glorifies God, and the rightly ordered person will see God's salvation
Salvation removes the need for praise
medium.explanation: The verse joins glorifying God through praise with seeing God's salvation.
medium.q: How are praise and salvation related?

answers: One forgets God, while the other glorifies Him and orders his conduct rightly
One offers praise and the other prays
One judges and the other witnesses
challenge.explanation: The passage contrasts forgetting God with praise, right conduct, and receiving salvation.
challenge.q: What is the main contrast between those who forget God and the person who offers praise?

answers: The person who orders his conduct rightly will see God's salvation
challenge.explanation: The verse connects ordering one's conversation aright with God's showing salvation.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between the right way and God's salvation?

answers: Those who forget God have no judgment
Praise and right conduct honor God and lead to seeing His salvation
challenge.explanation: The conclusion warns those who forget God and commends praise and rightly ordered conduct.
challenge.q: Which message best summarizes the passage?
